title: Proactive ingress shaping and kernel prefetch for embedding p99 stabilization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Production embedding endpoints are showing p99 spikes during bursty traffic and tenant mix changes. Root cause analysis points to a combination of: (1) micro-batches that interleave very short and long requests creating head-of-line blocking, (2) cold kernel context selection on GPUs for rare model variants, and (3) KV cache warmup gaps when tenant traffic hops between shards. Goal: Reduce embedding endpoint p99 from current baseline (~350ms) to <=180ms under 95th traffic patterns while keeping median latency stable and preserving throughput. This ticket implements a coordinated approach: proactive ingress shaping (quantile-based admission control + short-path fast lanes), a lightweight kernel prefetch probe that warms optimized kernels before dispatch, and an LRU-K inspired KV-cache warmup policy for tenant-level locality.
steps: Instrument per-request expected_execution_time (EET) estimator from historical traces (pipeline: length, model_variant, tenant_id) - engineer: Jonah
Implement ingress shaper that groups incoming requests by EET quantiles and enforces micro-batch composition constraints (min and max batch size per shard) - engineer: Jonah

Add kernel prefetch probe: when a model_variant is selected but not used recently, enqueue a 1-token synthetic probe to trigger optimized kernel selection without counting against customer quotas - engineer: Priya Desai
KV-cache LRU-K warmup: track last-K access timestamps per tenant-shard and prefill KV cache for hot tenants during burst ramp-ups - engineer: Marco Ruiz
Create canary rollout that seeds 5% of traffic from low-risk tenants to the new shaper+prefetch control plane in prod-staging - SRE: Elena
acceptance_criteria: p99 embedding endpoint latency <= 180ms on canary traffic (measured over 24h of representative burst tests)
Median latency change <= +10ms compared to baseline
Throughput (tokens/sec) drop <= 2% at 95th percentile traffic levels
No quota-visible synthetic probes charged to customers; probes tagged and excluded from billing
Sane fallback: when prefetch fails or causes regressions, system disables prefetch per-model-variant via feature flag in <15s
decisions: Use EET estimator (lightweight histogram model) instead of full ML predictor to keep CPU overhead <1% of ingress tier
Kernel prefetch will use synthetic 1-token requests and be marked with synthetic metadata; these are excluded from billing and tracing sample exports
Prefetch rate capped to 0.5 prefetch/sec per model-variant by default; can be tuned via runtime. This limits probe-induced noise.
Do NOT change default quantization or kernel selection heuristics in this ticket; we will only warm the existing optimized kernels to avoid changing inference outputs.
experiments: Exp A (staging): Ingress shaper only. Result: p99 reduced from 350ms -> 230ms for synthetic burst load (traffic mix A). Baseline run: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/ingress-shaper-staging?orgId=1
Exp B (staging): Kernel prefetch only. Result: p99 reduced to 210ms, but small increase in 50th (+6ms) due to probe interleaving. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321
Exp C (staging): Shaper + prefetch + KV warmup. Result: p99 stabilized at 165ms on representative burst tests (24h). Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/p99-stabilization?orgId=1
Perf regression tests: Batches/sec and tokens/sec measured in perf-cluster-7. No throughput regression > 1.6% observed under mixed-tenancy workload.
A/B canary in prod-staging started 2026-02-28 at 05:00 UTC: 5% traffic. Initial 12h results show p99 delta -35% for canary tenants; monitoring alert suppressed for first 6h while measuring stability.
notes: Telemetry: added ingress.eet, kernel.prefetch.count (tagged synthetic), kv.warmup.prefill_count. Telemetry docs: confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Prefetch+Telemetry
Cost: synthetic probes should be cheap; estimate additional GPU cycles <0.04% across fleet with default caps. Finance notified: finance@redwood.ai

SRE concerns: kernel prefetch creates additional small allocations; memory watchers must be enabled for the prefetch path. SRE runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=embedding-prefetch-runbook
Edge-case: model_variant churn can cause prefetch thrashing. Mitigation: cooldown per model_variant of 30s after prefetch attempt failure.
